thread:
eli: seeing ~30% throughput drop on prod-eu clusters starting ~08:12 UTC. Multiple worker restarts and a few GPU OOMs. Wasn't this quiet before the kernel selector rollout? anyone taking a look?

infra-bot: alert at 08:14 UTC - GPU_OOM on gpu-eu-12 (worker-42). restart_count=3, last_event=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

sana: saw a similar pattern in staging earlier today. profiler shows alloc churn spike and repeated cuMemGetInfo reports 'free=XXX MB' even though resident set not near GPU capacity. smells like fragmentation.

kyle: can you paste the OOM logs?

kyle: ```
[worker-42] ERROR: cuMemAlloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[worker-42] pid=4321 oom-kill: allocated 4096MB but free 128MB
[worker-42] runtime: falling back to host alloc -> slower path
```

jun: is this classic allocator fragmentation? remember we flipped allocator fallback toggles last week (rollout id 2026-03-09-optimizer-kernel-select). That change modified kernel selection and also toggled a small allocator path for some model shapes.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-09-optimizer-kernel-select -> prod-eu deployed at 07:50 UTC by kyle. config: kernel_selection_strategy=throughput_v2, allocator_fallback=auto.

sana: profiler snapshots: kv_cache_evictions/sec jumped from ~2 to ~48, avg batch_size dropped from 6.1 -> 1.2, p50 latency up 18%. When workers restart we lose in-flight batches and heuristics fall back to safety single-request batches. Combined with higher per-request alloc overhead this kills throughput.

eli: summary hypothesis: new kernel-selection + allocator fallback behaviour increases fragmentation/alloc failures -> GPU OOMs -> worker restarts -> batching heuristic collapses to size 1 -> throughput drop.

kyle: I can spin a revert for kernel_selection_strategy on prod-eu canary nodes. which exact flag to flip? looks like `kernel_selection_strategy=throughput_v2` was the change. revert to `throughput_v1`?

jun: before revert, quick mitigations: force enable `cudaMallocAsync=true` on the affected nodes to reduce fragmentation pressure, and throttle KV cache eviction by setting kv_cache_limit_mb=512 so we don't thrash. If throughput recovers, we still need heap-level tracing.

infra-bot: applied kv_cache_limit_mb=512 to gpu-eu-12 and gpu-eu-13 at 08:30 UTC. also toggled cudaMallocAsync=true on gpu-eu-13 for testing.

infra-bot: metrics update (08:40 UTC): worker restarts on gpu-eu-12 dropped to 0 in the last 10m, batch_size avg back to ~4.1, throughput restoring.

eli: good signal. rolling revert of kernel selector started at 08:45 UTC for 10% canary. early telemetry shows p50 latency stabilizing and no new OOMs on canary.

eli: next steps: 1) full revert if canary stable, 2) schedule allocator heap fragmentation trace (heapshot + cudaMallocAsync diff) on affected nodes, 3) modify batching heuristic to not collapse to size 1 on transient restarts (use short warmup sampling). I'll open follow-up ticket with traces. :thumbsup:
